title: ‘The Dog Stars’ Review: Jacob Elordi’s Sensitive Survivalist Can’t Sustain a Dreary Dystopian Adventure
content:
Four flu-pandemic survivors do the best they can in trying circumstances in Ridley Scott's low-energy latest, and the same goes for the charismatic quartet of actors muddling through it.

ByGuy Lodge

Film Critic

It’s the end of the world as we know it in “The Dog Stars,” and everyone feels — well, not fine exactly, but, you know,fine? Alive, hanging in there, taking it one day at a time. Things could be better, which goes without saying in the aftermath of a flu pandemic that has wiped out most of the planet’s human population, but the four principals here could also be dead, so there’s that. That shrugging, slightly bereft air of just-getting-by is the prevailing mood ofRidley Scott‘s post-apocalyptic survival story, and it’s a tough one to sustain dramatically, much less with any sense of intrepid adventure. Somewhat aptly released at the tail end of a long, loud movie summer, this is a surprisingly low-energy, low-incident blockbuster; you’d appreciate its mellow, character-oriented approach if it gave you any real characters to hold onto.

Peter Heller’s popular 2012 source novel largely did. Concentrated and eventful, it brought Jack London-style terseness and lyricism, as well as some mordant gallows humor, to the oft-solitary saga of Hig, a qualified mechanic eking out a life on an abandoned airstrip in rural Colorado, less than a decade after the fateful plague. (The year in the film is given, most pessimistically, as 2035. Start stockpiling now.) On the page, Hig’s first-person descriptions of his everyday adventures, and of the waning natural world around him, had an honest, melancholy soul to them. That voice doesn’t carry over to the adaptation by screenwriter Mark L. Smith — something of a specialist in survivalist drama, having also scripted “The Revenant” and “The Midnight Sky” — which forgoes narration altogether; the film bets onJacob Elordi‘s blokey, slightly sad-eyed charm to fill in the gaps.

It’s not a bad bet; it just doesn’t quite pay off. Elordi’s gift as a performer is for mining deeper seams of humanity in unappealing characters, from the douchey trust-fund scion of “Saltburn” to the literal monster of “Frankenstein.” Given a simply dull one, as he is here, he fares less well. The film’s Hig is nice; he’s admirably practical and resourceful; he looks terrific in weathered Carhartt workwear. But even handed the sympathetic accoutrements of a faithful German shepherd sidekick and repeated silent flashbacks to his deceased wife, he remains a bit of a blank. The film’s strangely lackadaisical opening act, heavy on scenes of Hig flying his battered Cessna alone, desperately needs the gruff friction provided byJosh Brolinas Bangley, his fellow survivor turned reluctant platonic life partner.

Hig and Bangley have an established routine that keeps them alive, if not all that elated to be so. Hig regularly flies to Denver, now a bombed-out ghost town, to pick up supplies from sundry abandoned stores, bars and hospitals. On their compound, they alternate guard duty, on the alert for sporadic bands of intruders, whom Bangley insists be shot on sight. When Hig can’t take it anymore, desperate for any kind of escape, he winds up crash-landing his plane near the spartan farm of grizzled rancher Jack (Guy Pearce) and his lonely daughter Cima (Margaret Qualley), whose routine is similarly, joylessly focused on existence and endurance: The grass, of course, is always greener on the other side of the Rockies. A thin romance ensues. The dramatic tempo stays much the same.

At its most interesting, “The Dog Stars” mimics the structure and stakes of a classic frontier Western, echoed quite literally in its two liveliest action setpieces: a briefly spectacular yet unperilous buffalo stampede, and a faceoff with a marauding tribe of feral, thickly made-up men on horseback, rather incuriously positioned by the film as an outright enemy force. The old-fashioned cowboys-and-Indians dynamic of this sequence is hard to ignore, as is the shared whiteness of the film’s leading characters: In this dog-eat-dog world, whose brutal survival strategies get to be heroic, and why?

Smith’s spare, episodic script doesn’t risk such introspection, or indeed much else — save for one whopper of a departure from the novel, late in the proceedings, that sharply wrests the tone from ruggedly earnest wilderness drama to macabre, borderline-camp horror-comedy, only to reverse course so abruptly you wonder if either you or the film dropped out for a quick fever-dream. It certainly yanks your attention amid the generally homey, lolloping rhythm of the film. It also more or less demolishes whatever credibility this future-rustic story world has built up to this point. In this case, Scott’s famously catholic genre interests come at some cost to the integrity of the whole enterprise; you sense he might feel as impatient with these sturdy, morose, faintly drab characters as we do.

All four stars ably play the stoic and sorrowful notes required of them, without finding many secondary or contrasting ones in their dialogue. “The Dog Stars” winds up coasting on their collective capabilities and charisma, as well as on Scott’s autopilot proficiency. If the tirelessly prolific director never seems more than intermittently invested in this material, the strongest passages here thrive on his muscular command of scale, and he can still pick a landscape with the best of them: Northern Italy fills in robustly for the Centennial State here, even though Erik Messerschmidt’s consistently charcoal-washed lensing suggests there’s no magic hour in this unforgiving dystopia. This isn’t a future to be prettified, and fair enough, but that impulse also falls in line with the film’s stubbornly un-fun, eat-your-greens demeanor: Can’tsomethinghere thrive rather than survive?
title_zh: 《狗之星(The Dog Stars)》影評：雅各布·艾洛迪(Jacob Elordi)的敏感生存者無法支撐這場沉悶的反烏托邦冒險
content_zh:
在雷德利·史考特(Ridley Scott)的最新作品中，四位流感大流行的倖存者在艱難的環境中竭盡所能，而這也適用於這四位魅力四射的演員們在其中的掙扎。

文／蓋·洛奇(Guy Lodge)

影評人

在《狗之星》(The Dog Stars)中，這是我們所知的世界的終結，每個人都感受到——嗯，並不完全好，但，你知道的，還算可以？活著，堅持著，一天一天地過去。情況本可以更好，這在流感大流行之後幾乎是顯而易見的，這場疫情已經摧毀了地球上大部分的人口，但這裡的四位主角也可能已經死去，所以至少還有這一點。那種略顯失落的勉強過活的氛圍是雷德利·史考特的末日生存故事的主流情緒，而這在戲劇上維持起來相當困難，更不用說帶有任何勇敢冒險的感覺了。這部電影在漫長而喧鬧的夏季電影季末期上映，意外地成為一部低能量、低事件的大片；如果它能給你一些真正的角色讓你依附，你會欣賞它那種平和、以角色為導向的方式。

彼得·海勒(Peter Heller)於2012年出版的熱門小說在這方面做得相當好。它集中且充滿事件，帶來了傑克·倫敦(Jack London)式的簡潔和抒情，以及一些尖刻的絞刑幽默，講述了希格(Hig)的孤獨故事，這位合格的技工在命運多舛的疫情後不到十年，勉強在科羅拉多州一條廢棄的跑道上生活。（電影中的年份最悲觀地設定為2035年。趕緊開始囤積吧。）在書中，希格以第一人稱描述他日常冒險的方式，以及他周圍逐漸消逝的自然世界，充滿了真誠而憂傷的靈魂。這種聲音並未在編劇馬克·L·史密斯(Mark L. Smith)的改編中延續——他在生存主題劇情方面頗有專長，曾編劇《大地驚雷》(The Revenant)和《午夜天空》(The Midnight Sky)——該片完全放棄了旁白；電影寄希望於雅各布·艾洛迪(Jacob Elordi)那種略顯憂傷的魅力來填補空白。

這不是一個壞的賭注；只是沒有完全奏效。艾洛迪作為演員的天賦在於能夠在不討喜的角色中挖掘更深層次的人性，從《鹽灘》(Saltburn)中的富二代到《科學怪人》(Frankenstein)中的字面怪物。給他一個簡單乏味的角色，如今這裡的希格，他的表現就不太理想。電影中的希格很友善；他實際上非常務實和足智多謀；他穿著風化的卡哈特(Carahart)工作服看起來很棒。但即使擁有忠實的德國牧羊犬夥伴和對已故妻子的重複無聲回憶，他仍然顯得有些空洞。電影奇怪地懶散的開場部分，重重地描繪了希格獨自駕駛他那架破舊的塞斯納(Cessna)飛行的場景，迫切需要喬什·布洛林(Josh Brolin)飾演的班格利(Bangley)所提供的粗獷摩擦，班格利是他的倖存夥伴，最終成為不情願的柏拉圖式生活伴侶。

《狗星(The Dog Stars)》的故事圍繞著希格(Hig)和班利(Bangley)的日常生活，他們的例行公事讓他們活著，儘管並不特別快樂。希格定期飛往丹佛(Denver)，這個如今已成為被轟炸的鬼城，從各種被遺棄的商店、酒吧和醫院中收集物資。在他們的基地裡，他們輪流值班，隨時警惕偶爾出現的入侵者，班利堅持要對這些入侵者立即開火。當希格再也忍受不了，渴望任何形式的逃脫時，他最終在粗獷的牧場主傑克(Jack)（蓋·皮爾斯(Guy Pearce)）和他孤獨的女兒西瑪(Cima)（瑪格·羅比(Margaret Qualley)）的簡陋農場附近迫降了他的飛機。西瑪的生活同樣是毫無快樂地專注於生存和忍耐：畢竟，洛基山脈那邊的草總是更綠一些。隨之而來的是一段微薄的浪漫。整體的戲劇節奏保持著相似的風格。

在《狗星》中最有趣的部分是，它模仿了經典邊境西部片的結構和風險，這在兩個最生動的動作場景中得到了字面上的回響：一場短暫壯觀但並不危險的水牛奔逃，以及與一群騎馬的野蠻部落的對峙，這些部落的男性化妝濃厚，電影將他們明確地定位為敵對勢力。這段情節中老式的牛仔與印第安人的動態難以忽視，影片的主要角色也共享著白人身份：在這個弱肉強食的世界裡，誰的殘酷生存策略能被視為英雄，為什麼？

史密斯(Smith)的簡約、分段式劇本並未冒險進行這種內省，或實際上其他的事情——除了在故事進行到後期時，從小說中大幅偏離的一個重大轉折，這個轉折將基調從堅韌誠懇的荒野劇轉變為陰森、邊緣化的恐怖喜劇，卻又如此突然地逆轉，讓你懷疑自己或電影是否在短暫的發燒夢中掉隊。這無疑在影片整體溫馨、悠閒的節奏中吸引了你的注意力。這也幾乎摧毀了這個未來鄉村故事世界到目前為止所建立的任何可信度。在這種情況下，斯科特(Scott)著名的廣泛類型興趣對整個作品的完整性造成了一定的損失；你能感受到他可能對這些堅韌、陰鬱、略顯沉悶的角色感到和我們一樣的不耐煩。

四位明星都能出色地詮釋出所需的冷靜與悲傷的情感，然而在對話中並未找到太多的次要或對比的情緒。《狗星(Dog Stars)》最終依賴於他們的集體能力和魅力，以及導演斯科特·德瑞克森(Scott Derrickson)的自動駕駛式專業。如果這位不知疲倦的高產導演似乎對這部作品的投入僅僅是間歇性的，那麼這裡最強的片段則依賴於他對規模的強有力掌控，他仍然能夠挑選出最美的風景：北義大利在這裡強而有力地替代了百年州，儘管埃里克·梅塞施密特(Erik Messerschmidt)持續的木炭色調鏡頭暗示著在這個無情的反烏托邦中並不存在魔法時刻。這不是一個可以被美化的未來，這也無可厚非，但這種衝動也符合影片固執地不尋求娛樂、要你吃青菜的風格：難道這裡不能繁榮而非僅僅生存嗎？

文／蓋·洛奇(Guy Lodge)

影評人

在《狗之星》(The Dog Stars)中，這是我們所知的世界的終結，每個人都感受到——嗯，並不完全好，但，你知道的，還算可以？活著，堅持著，一天一天地過去。
